exposure: prenatal perfluorine and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure (PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFHxA)
outcome: infant neurodevelopmental delay (assessed by ASQ-3 score)
cohort: The study included 2415 mother-newborn pairs from the China WuHu Birth Cohort Study (WH-BC).
finding: Prenatal PFAS exposure was associated with infant developmental delays, with gender differences observed, and these delays could be attenuated by postnatal DHA supplementation.
